name: Houston
metaDescription: Industry-specific market reports for Houston, Texas. Landscaping, roofing, HVAC, and pest control intelligence with local demand, pricing, and competitive data.
ogDescription: Local market reports for Houston operators — demand, competition, pricing, and growth opportunities by industry.
intro: Houston's heat and humidity make it one of the highest-recurring-revenue home-services metros in the country. HVAC service plans, mosquito subscriptions, and lawn maintenance contracts attach at rates that operators in cooler markets don't see.
statsSource: Population and households: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 1-year estimates for the metro area. Business count: Sherlock Research estimate.
reportsIntro: Each Sherlock industry report includes a city-specific data cut for Houston — local demand, competitor density, pricing benchmarks, and neighborhood-level demand patterns. Houston's climate drives year-round demand for outdoor services and recurring pest, HVAC, and lawn care.

reportBlurbs.landscaping: Residential and commercial landscape services in Houston: demand drivers, top zip codes, pricing tiers, and competitive landscape.
reportBlurbs.roofing: Roofing market intelligence for Houston: storm cycles, insurance dynamics, reroof rates, and local competitor positioning.
reportBlurbs.hvac: HVAC service and install market for Houston: heat-pump adoption, service-plan pricing, refrigerant transition impact.
reportBlurbs.pest-control: Recurring pest control market in Houston: subscription rates, residential vs commercial mix, and local consolidation dynamics.

insights.title: Year-round service demand
insights.text: Mild winters mean lawn care, pest, and HVAC service plans run 12 months — not 8 like in the north. Recurring revenue mix here is 15%+ higher than the national average.

insights.title: Hurricane & storm prep
insights.text: Annual hurricane season creates predictable demand for roofing inspections, tree services, and generator installs from May through October.

insights.title: Energy-sector economic cycles
insights.text: Houston's economy still tracks oil prices — the high end of the market expands and contracts faster than other Texas metros.
